title: Lock Desk Note: Closing Reach of a Relocked Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
A relock of a Builder Extended Rate Lock runs a fixed number of days, and a scheduled closing that falls after the relocked lock ends is priced into the relock fee percent.

**Rule.** The closing overhang is the calendar days by which the purchase agreement's scheduled closing date falls after the relock date plus the term's relock term days. An overhang above 15 days adds 0.125 percentage points to the relock fee percent; an overhang of one day up to 15 days adds 0.0625 percentage points; no overhang adds nothing. The points are added to the relock fee percent before that percent is applied to the loan amount on the lock.

## Relock term days used in the overhang

| Lock term | Relock term days |
|---|---|
| 60-Day Standard Lock | 30 |
| 90-Day Lock | 30 |
| 120-Day Extended Lock | 30 |
| 180-Day Extended Lock | 30 |
| 270-Day Build Lock | 45 |
| 360-Day Build Lock | 45 |

## Overhang bands

| Closing overhang | Added to the relock fee percent |
|---|---|
| none — the scheduled closing date is on or before the relock date plus the relock term days | nothing |
| 1 to 15 days | 0.0625 percentage points |
| 16 days or more | 0.125 percentage points |

The scheduled closing date is read from the Home Purchase Agreement record of the agreement the lock finances.

## Worked example (hypothetical dates)

A 90-Day Lock relocked on 2 June: the relock date plus 30 days is 2 July. A scheduled closing date of 17 July gives an overhang of 15 days and adds 0.0625 points; 18 July gives 16 days and adds 0.125 points; 30 June gives no overhang and adds nothing.
